title: CDA-GNN: A Chain-driven Accelerator for Efficient Asynchronous Graph Neural Network
problem: Asynchronous Graph Neural Networks suffer from redundant computation overhead and excessive off-chip communications due to irregular state propagations along dependency chains between vertices. Existing software and hardware solutions fail to efficiently handle these irregular patterns.
motivation: Asynchronous GNNs enable faster convergence than synchronous GNNs, making efficiency improvements critical for practical large-scale deployment.
method: Graph neural networks propagate information along chains of connected nodes, and these patterns can be exploited. CDA-GNN organizes computation around chain-driven execution: instead of updating each node independently (which repeats work), it regularizes when nodes update to align with dependency chains, eliminating wasted calculations and off-chip memory transfers. This is implemented on a Xilinx Alveo U280 FPGA with chain-aware data caching (keeping data near the processor based on node dependencies) and optimized dataflow scheduling (delivering data exactly when computation needs it).
key_novelty: Chain-driven asynchronous execution that regularizes state propagations along dependency chains, eliminating redundant computation and off-chip memory traffic.
contributions: Chain-driven asynchronous execution methodology for AGNN that regularizes irregular vertex state propagations
Chain-aware data caching technique to maximize data locality in AGNN workloads
FPGA-based accelerator achieving up to 1,173x speedup and 2,241x energy savings over software solutions
Demonstrated superiority over state-of-the-art hardware accelerators with 7.9x-10.2x performance improvements
primary_theme: FPGA acceleration for asynchronous GNN inference via chain-driven execution
